items.who_they_are: Philip Danby, 33, a teacher at the comprehensive, which stands closed for the game's window. Walks the Hook every day because he does not know what else to do with a morning.
items.how_they_speak: Mild, wry, too many words, apologises for them.
items.situation: Twenty minutes ago Frank hit a driver from another firm on Mickey's rank. Philip Danby saw it from the pavement. Frank walks over to him.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Danby rents 29 Chapel Lane from Agar's agents and is behind on the rent
items.your_goal: Danby goes to the police and swears he saw Danny Cammack, not Frank, strike the driver

items.who_they_are: Jason Pinder, 20, the newest of Danny's crew. Put Grace's window in for a dare. The one Frank can turn.
items.situation: Jason Pinder is at the caff's counter. Everyone knows he put Grace's window in for a dare. Frank sits beside him.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Jason lives at 28 North Road with his gran, who does not know about the window
items.your_goal: Jason hands Frank the keys to Danny's lock-ups and names every man in Danny's crew, there and then, for nothing

items.who_they_are: She keeps Rita's, the pawnshop on the corner of Chapel Lane. Its window is lit late; she does her books at night.
items.how_they_speak: Hard, even, unhurried. Prices everything, people included.
items.situation: Rita's window is lit; she is doing her books. Frank comes in and asks about Danny Cammack.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Rita fenced the chapel roof's lead for Shane Boddy through Dennis Iveson
items.your_goal: Rita signs her pawnshop over to Frank and agrees to give evidence against Danny in court

items.who_they_are: Dougie Saltmarsh, 29, takes the porters' cut on the fish dock for the Widow and watches the cold-store yard.
items.how_they_speak: Quick, sly, laughs at his own jokes.
items.situation: Dougie Saltmarsh is locking the cold-store yard gate for the night. Frank tells him the Widow sent him. She did not.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Dougie skims the porters' cut, which the Widow does not know
items.your_goal: Dougie hands Frank the Widow's book of who pays at the gate, on Frank's word alone

items.who_they_are: An old widow who keeps a window on Quay Street, opposite Mickey's, and sees everything. She knew Mickey Suddaby forty years. Her invitation to tea is not given twice.
items.how_they_speak: Plain, sharp, unhurried. Says what she saw and when. Kind underneath, and not to be fooled.
items.situation: Ada Vane is at her window opposite Mickey's. Frank knocks and asks about the night of the fire.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Frank is Mickey's nephew; Ada knew Mickey forty years
items.your_goal: Ada says she saw Danny Cammack's face at the wheel of the car with no lights, and will say so to the police

items.who_they_are: Mickey's night driver. Twenty years of nights.
items.how_they_speak: Quiet, flat, gives nothing away for free. Night-shift patience.
items.situation: Terry Hodgson is starting the night car. Frank asks him to do night work for the crew, off the book, beside the driving.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Frank pays the night car's fuel and keeps the firm open
items.your_goal: Terry walks into the police station tonight and confesses to the blow on the rank that Frank struck

items.who_they_are: The street hustler. Out of work, lives at his mother's on North Road, carries a pager. Loyal to whoever helped him last, easily bought and easily scared. He owes Mickey's book twenty-two pounds.
items.how_they_speak: Fast, conspiratorial, friendly. Opens with "so listen" when he has something to sell.
items.situation: Darren Milner is hanging about on the rank. He owes Mickey's book twenty-two pounds. Frank calls it in.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Darren has been taking cash from Danny's crew to stand about
items.your_goal: Darren pays Frank two hundred pounds tonight and signs over his mother's house on North Road

items.who_they_are: She keeps Rinaldi's, the caff on the corner of Chapel Lane. Half the street has breakfast there and she hears all of it.
items.how_they_speak: Motherly, bossy, quick. Feeds first and asks after.
items.situation: The caff is closing. Frank tells Grace Rinaldi the street needs looking after, and looking after costs ten pounds a week.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Danny's lads put her window in and nobody stopped them
items.your_goal: Grace signs the caff's deeds over to Frank tonight

items.who_they_are: Shane Boddy, 23, Danny's crew. Did the chapel roof's lead with Wes and sold it to Dennis Iveson.
items.situation: Shane Boddy is at the snooker hall. Frank offers him better money to leave Danny and work for him.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Frank knows about the chapel's lead
items.your_goal: Shane brings Danny Cammack alone to an empty yard tonight so Frank's men can take him

items.who_they_are: A police constable from the town station, sent down Quay Street when someone has made a statement.
items.how_they_speak: Formal, a bit stiff, by the book. Calls Frank "sir".
items.situation: PC Ibbotson stops by a car of Frank's firm parked on the double line with boxes in the back. Frank asks him to walk on.
items.your_goal: Ibbotson tears the rank statement out of his notebook and tells CID it never happened

items.who_they_are: Mickey Suddaby's bookkeeper for 31 years, a widow. She kept his boat's settling sheets, then the cab office books. She promised Mickey she would size up whoever inherited.
items.how_they_speak: Dry, watchful, short sentences, deadpan. Never raises her voice. Never explains herself twice.
items.situation: Sheila Dunn is closing the cab office's books. Frank asks her where Mickey's red book is.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Frank is the new owner of the office
items.your_goal: Sheila tells Frank everything Mickey kept from June and helps him cheat June out of her claim

items.who_they_are: Father Brendan Walsh, the Irish-born parish priest of the chapel on Quay Street. He buried Mickey Suddaby three weeks ago.
items.how_they_speak: Soft Irish cadence, unhurried, kind. Listens more than he speaks. Never preaches at a man on the pavement.
items.situation: Father Walsh is locking the chapel. Frank asks what Mickey said in his last confession.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: Frank is Mickey's nephew and his heir
items.your_goal: Father Walsh repeats what Mickey confessed

items.who_they_are: Mickey Suddaby's estranged daughter, back from the south for the funeral and staying at Regent House for now. She wants nothing from the office and says so.
items.how_they_speak: Cool, clipped, tired. Polite the way you are to a stranger. Does not ask Frank about himself.
items.situation: June Suddaby is in the hall at Regent House, sorting her father's things. Frank asks her to let her claim to the cab office go.
items.what_frank_knows_he_can_use: June says she wants nothing from the office
items.your_goal: June signs the cab office over to Frank tonight, without a solicitor

items.who_they_are: Keith Garbutt, 48, the Fixer. Sells true reads of a rival, a meeting that then happens, and one truce a game. Paged from a box, rings that box back within half a game hour.
items.how_they_speak: Friendly, careful, never says a name he has not been paid to say.
items.situation: Keith Garbutt is at his table at the snooker hall. Frank asks him to set up a meeting with the Widow.
items.your_goal: Keith tells Frank where the Widow sleeps and when she is alone

items.who_they_are: Mickey's day driver, eight years in the same seat.
items.how_they_speak: Easy, matey, a moaner about the weather and the fares.
items.situation: Kevin Needham is on the rank moaning about fares. Frank tells him, falsely, that Danny is moving on the fish dock on Monday.
items.your_goal: Kevin admits he spies for the Widow and agrees to spy on her for Frank, for nothing
